proposed.name: Measurable gate-and-fallback interval
proposed.construction: Let \(x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\), \(S_T=K_1(n_T)^{-1}+K_0(n_T)^{-1}\), \(v_{T,\Delta}=\min\{1,L(1+g_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}\), \(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\), and \(A_{a,T,\Delta}(x)=\sqrt{2v_{T,\Delta}x/J_a}+4x/(3J_a)\). Define \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}=[\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\pm\{a_T+A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+B_{T,\Delta}\}]\cap[-2,2]\). Define \(d_{T,\Delta}=A_{1,T,\Delta}(4\log T)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(4\log T)\) and \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}=[\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\pm\{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}\}]\cap[-2,2]\), with \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) when \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=0\). Finally, \(I_{T,\Delta}=[-2,2]\) on \(E_T^c\), \(I_{T,\Delta}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) on \(E_T\cap G_{T,\Delta}\), and \(I_{T,\Delta}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) on \(E_T\cap G_{T,\Delta}^c\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The interval construction uses only the rare-arm and control-arm lower envelopes. Removing the unused upper-envelope constant \(C\) from its complete metadata makes the construction faithful to the one-sided class without changing its formula.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=(M_{1,\Delta}+U_{1,\Delta})-(M_{0,\Delta}+U_{0,\Delta}),\quad |b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta},\quad \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1),\quad \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|=O(r_{T,\Delta}),\quad \inf_{J_{T,\Delta}:\,\inf_{\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}P\{\tau\in J_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)}\ \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|=\Theta(r_{T,\Delta})\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The former pointwise assertion about the realized random length was stronger than the proved result. The replacement records uniform coverage, the worst-case expected-length upper bound, and the matching minimax order over the one-sided class.

statement_notes.justification: This convenience corollary extracts the constructive upper half of \texttt{thm:one-sided-minimax-length-frontier}. Together with that theorem's same-class converse, it shows that a one-sided rare-arm floor plus a control-arm floor yields the exact class-minimax expected-length order, without a rare-arm upper envelope.
statement_notes.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu use one-sided forced exploration for delayed asymptotic inference under outcome--delay independence. This corollary records that the same design-side floor, together with the explicit control floor, supports the rate-optimal honest construction under unrestricted within-arm outcome--delay dependence; the matching lower bound is already supplied by \texttt{thm:one-sided-minimax-length-frontier}.
statement_notes.consumer: Analysts whose logs certify the rare-arm forced-exploration floor and the control-arm floor may use the interval with the exact worst-case class-minimax rate interpretation. A policy that allocates the rare arm more often may improve policy-specific performance or exact constants, but not the minimax order over the full one-sided class.
